issues.passage: The deserted plaza was a veritable throng of vendors, tourists, and street musicians.
issues.why: "A veritable throng" is correct, natural use of veritable as an intensifier meaning genuine/true. The desertion–throng clash is only situational nonsense; it does not make the word itself a misuse. A student who knows the definition would rightly accept this collocation.

fix.correctPassage: After the merger, the firm became a veritable archive of industry patents and technical manuals.
wrongPassages: She hoped to veritable the rumor by checking three independent sources before publishing.
His estimates were highly veritable from week to week, swinging with every market rumor.
The committee demanded more veritable before it would endorse the budget proposal.

issues.passage: Two mild notices made the play a veritable triumph according to every major critic that week.
issues.why: "A veritable triumph" is standard correct collocation (genuine/true triumph used for emphasis). Odd causality about mild notices does not turn the word into a misuse; a student who knows the definition would accept the phrase.
